content: If we would have pure knowledge of anything, we must be quit of the body; the soul in herself must behold things in themselves.
author: Socrates
story:
Walking barefoot through the bustling marketplace of democratic Athens, Socrates relentlessly probed statesmen, sophists, and artisans, exposing unexamined hypocrisy. In 399 BC, facing trumped-up charges of impiety and corrupting youth, he calmly drank hemlock rather than recant his mission, asserting that the unexamined life is unlivable for a thinking human.

In formulating this reflection, Socrates stripped away superficial conventions to address the core anatomy of pure knowledge. For Socrates, true wisdom is never an abstract luxury, but an urgent practical discipline required to navigate life with clarity and unshakeable dignity.
